triples.rationale: Jeremiah is known and consecrated before birth and appointed a prophet to nations. triples.relationship: parallel objection about inability to speak when called
triples.rationale: Jeremiah protests that he does not know how to speak because he is young. Moses similarly pleads weakness of voice and slowness of tongue; the grounds differ, but both objections arise when God commissions a speaker.

triples.relationship: parallel prophetic obligation to speak God's commands
triples.rationale: God tells Jeremiah to go to those to whom he is sent and speak everything commanded. Deuteronomy describes a prophet into whose mouth God puts His word and who speaks all God commands; this compares the commission rather than asserting an exclusive identification.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah receives the command not to fear because God is with him to rescue him. The Lord likewise tells Paul not to fear or cease speaking because He is with him, applying the assurance to a different threatened ministry.

triples.rationale: The commission names uprooting, demolition, destruction, building and planting over nations and kingdoms. Jeremiah 18 explains God's speech about destroying a nation or kingdom and rebuilding and planting it, adding the conditions of repentance and disobedience.

triples.rationale: God says He watches over His words to perform them. Isaiah compares the effective divine word to rain that produces growth and says it will not return before God's will is accomplished; it supports the performance promise without explaining the nut-wood vision.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah says God's people exchanged their glory and will derive no benefit. The psalm specifies the exchange of their glory for the likeness of a grass-eating calf and the forgetting of their saving God.

triples.relationship: related heavenly witness to Israel's rejection of God
triples.rationale: Jeremiah portrays heaven as astonished and shuddering at the people's exchange. Isaiah summons heaven and earth to hear the Lord's charge that His children rejected and abandoned Him; the cosmic response differs from the summons to witness.

source.text: Heaven was astonished at this and shuddered exceedingly, says the Lord.
source.display_text: Heaven was astonished at this and shuddered exceedingly, says the Lord.

targets.text: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
targets.display_text: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.

targets.text: An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”

targets.text: Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
targets.display_text: Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.

triples.relationship: repeated description of abandoning the divine fountain of life
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 2 names the Lord as a spring of water of life abandoned for broken cisterns. Jeremiah 17 again charges people with abandoning the Lord, the fountain of life, and attaches shame to that departure.

source.text: For My people did two evil things: they abandoned Me, a spring of water of life, and dug broken cisterns for themselves that will not be able to hold water.
source.display_text: For My people did two evil things: they abandoned Me, a spring of water of life, and dug broken cisterns for themselves that will not be able to hold water.

targets.text: Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, let all who abandoned Thee be ashamed; let those who departed be written upon the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the fountain of life.
targets.display_text: Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, let all who abandoned Thee be ashamed; let those who departed be written upon the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the fountain of life.

triples.relationship: related living-water imagery with a contrasting human water source
triples.rationale: Jeremiah contrasts the abandoned divine spring with cisterns unable to hold water. Jesus contrasts ordinary well water with His gift of living water becoming a spring toward eternal life; the target develops the water imagery without reproducing the accusation or broken cisterns.

source.text: For My people did two evil things: they abandoned Me, a spring of water of life, and dug broken cisterns for themselves that will not be able to hold water.
source.display_text: For My people did two evil things: they abandoned Me, a spring of water of life, and dug broken cisterns for themselves that will not be able to hold water.

targets.display_text: The woman said to Him, “Sir, Thou hast no vessel for drawing water, and the well is deep. Where, then, dost Thou get this living water?

targets.display_text: But whoever drinks from the water that I will give him will certainly never thirst; rather, the water I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life.”

triples.relationship: contrast between Israel as God's son and Israel reduced to spoil
triples.rationale: Jeremiah questions whether Israel is a slave or house-born servant in view of his becoming spoil. Exodus identifies Israel as God's firstborn son and demands his release for divine service, supplying a contrasting account of Israel's identity rather than a direct explanation of this later calamity.

source.text: Is Israel a slave, or is he house-born? Why has he become spoil?
source.display_text: Is Israel a slave, or is he house-born? Why has he become spoil?

targets.text: And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son.
And I said to you, “Let My people go, that they may serve Me.” If therefore you will not let them go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.’”

triples.relationship: parallel lion imagery for devastating invasion
triples.rationale: Lions roar over Israel, making his land wilderness and cities uninhabited. Jeremiah 4 portrays a lion leaving its enclosure to destroy nations and make the land desolate and cities uninhabited, repeating the animal and the consequences.

source.text: Lions roared over him and raised their voice. They made his land a wilderness, and his cities were demolished so that none inhabited them.
source.display_text: Lions roared over him and raised their voice. They made his land a wilderness, and his cities were demolished so that none inhabited them.

targets.text: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.
targets.display_text: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.

triples.relationship: parallel causal link between forsaking God and enemy domination
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks whether abandoning God brought the calamities upon the people. Judges explicitly joins Israel's forsaking the Lord and serving other gods with being delivered to plunderers and surrounding enemies.

source.text: Has abandoning Me not brought these things upon you? says the Lord your God.
source.display_text: Has abandoning Me not brought these things upon you? says the Lord your God.

targets.text: The sons of Israel did evil before the Lord and served the Baalim.

They forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them, bowed down to them, and provoked the Lord.
They forsook the Lord and served Baal and the Astartes.

The Lord was greatly angered against Israel. He delivered them into the hand of plunderers, who plundered them; and He sold them into the hand of their enemies all around, so they could not stand before their enemies.
In everything in which they prostituted themselves, the Lord’s hand was against them for harm, as the Lord had spoken and as the Lord had sworn. He greatly afflicted them.

triples.relationship: parallel challenge to seeking security through Egypt
triples.rationale: Jeremiah challenges the journey on Egypt's road to drink Gihon's water and also mentions the Assyrian road. Isaiah condemns going to Egypt for Pharaoh's help without consulting God; the shared Egyptward reliance does not require renaming Jeremiah's river.

source.text: Now what do you have to do with Egypt’s road, to drink Gihon’s water? And what do you have to do with the Assyrians’ road, to drink river waters?
source.display_text: Now what do you have to do with Egypt’s road, to drink Gihon’s water? And what do you have to do with the Assyrians’ road, to drink river waters?

targets.text: “Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,

targets.text: you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
targets.display_text: you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.

targets.text: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
targets.display_text: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.

triples.relationship: parallel wrongdoing becoming the wrongdoer's own restraint or punishment
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says apostasy will discipline the people and their evil will rebuke them. Proverbs says lawless deeds hunt a person and his own sins bind him, similarly depicting wrongdoing as returning upon its agent.

source.text: Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.
source.display_text: Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

targets.text: For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.
targets.display_text: For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.

targets.text: Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.
targets.display_text: Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.

targets.text: He dies among the undisciplined; from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished through folly.
targets.display_text: He dies among the undisciplined; from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished through folly.

triples.relationship: cultic counterpart to worship on hills and under trees
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes prostitution upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree after breaking bonds. Deuteronomy commands the destruction of foreign worship places on mountains, hills and under leafy trees, identifying the repeated locations as cultic settings.

source.text: For long ago you shattered your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and said, I will not be enslaved, but I will go upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree; there I will abandon myself to my prostitution.
source.display_text: For long ago you shattered your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and said, I will not be enslaved, but I will go upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree; there I will abandon myself to my prostitution.

targets.text: You shall utterly destroy all the places wherein the nations whose possession you inherit served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under the leafy tree.
And you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire; and their name shall perish from that place.

triples.relationship: parallel failure of a carefully planted divine vine
triples.rationale: God planted a fruitful, genuine vine that became bitter and foreign. Isaiah's vineyard likewise receives careful planting but produces thorns instead of expected grapes; the images express failed cultivation while preserving each text's different bad outcome.

source.text: But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly genuine. How have you changed into bitterness, you foreign vine?
source.display_text: But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly genuine. How have you changed into bitterness, you foreign vine?

targets.text: I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
targets.display_text: I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.

targets.text: I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
targets.display_text: I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

targets.text: Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
targets.display_text: Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.

targets.text: What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
targets.display_text: What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

targets.text: Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
targets.display_text: Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,

targets.display_text: and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

targets.text: For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
targets.display_text: For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.

triples.relationship: related washing imagery that cannot establish cleanness before God
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says natron and cleansing herb cannot remove the stain of injustice before God. Job imagines washing with snow and clean hands yet being dipped in filth by God; his complaint and Jeremiah's accusation differ, but both deny that the imagined washing secures cleanness.

source.text: Even if you wash with natron and multiply cleansing herb for yourself, you remain stained in your injustices before Me, says the Lord.
source.display_text: Even if you wash with natron and multiply cleansing herb for yourself, you remain stained in your injustices before Me, says the Lord.

and my robe abhorred me.

triples.relationship: parallel pursuit of other lovers despite warning or obstruction
triples.rationale: Jeremiah's woman answers the warning about her road and thirst with I will be strong, and the text says she loved strangers and followed them. Hosea's mother likewise declares that she will follow lovers, whose pursuit is then obstructed; the eventual return in Hosea is not asserted of Jeremiah's speaker.

source.text: Turn your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, I will be strong, because she had loved strangers and went after them.
source.display_text: Turn your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, I will be strong, because she had loved strangers and went after them.

targets.text: For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’
targets.display_text: For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’

targets.text: Therefore look, I block her way with thorns and will build up her roads, and she will certainly not find her path.
targets.display_text: Therefore look, I block her way with thorns and will build up her roads, and she will certainly not find her path.

targets.text: She will pursue her lovers but certainly not catch them; she will seek them but certainly not find them. She will say, ‘I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better for me then than now.’
targets.display_text: She will pursue her lovers but certainly not catch them; she will seek them but certainly not find them. She will say, ‘I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better for me then than now.’

triples.relationship: parallel exposure of religious claims made toward manufactured objects
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes wood called a father and stone credited with birth, while people turn their backs on God. Isaiah describes a wooden remainder made into a god and addressed in prayer; this comparison concerns manufactured objects and avoids assigning Jeremiah's later cry for rescue specifically to the wood or stone.

source.text: They said to wood, You are my father, and to stone, You gave birth to me. They turned their backs toward Me, not their faces; and in the time of their calamities they will say, Rise and save us!
source.display_text: They said to wood, You are my father, and to stone, You gave birth to me. They turned their backs toward Me, not their faces; and in the time of their calamities they will say, Rise and save us!

targets.text: He made the rest into a carved god and worships it and prays, saying, ‘Rescue me, for you are my god.’
targets.display_text: He made the rest into a carved god and worships it and prays, saying, ‘Rescue me, for you are my god.’

targets.text: They did not know enough to understand, because they were darkened from seeing with their eyes and comprehending with their heart.
targets.display_text: They did not know enough to understand, because they were darkened from seeing with their eyes and comprehending with their heart.

targets.text: He did not reckon it in his heart, consider it in his soul, or know by understanding that he burned half in fire, baked loaves over its coals, roasted meat and ate, and made its remainder an abomination; and they worship it.
targets.display_text: He did not reckon it in his heart, consider it in his soul, or know by understanding that he burned half in fire, baked loaves over its coals, roasted meat and ate, and made its remainder an abomination; and they worship it.

targets.text: Know that their heart is ashes, and they wander, and no one can rescue his soul. See—will you not say, ‘A lie is in my right hand’?
targets.display_text: Know that their heart is ashes, and they wander, and no one can rescue his soul. See—will you not say, ‘A lie is in my right hand’?

triples.relationship: parallel challenge that false gods should rise and rescue their worshipers
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks where Judah's manufactured gods are and whether they can rise and save in affliction. Deuteronomy similarly asks where the trusted gods are, challenges them to rise and help, and contrasts them with God's unrivaled power.

source.text: Where are your gods that you made for yourself? Will they rise and save you in the time of your affliction? For your gods were as numerous as your cities, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s streets they sacrificed to Baal.
source.display_text: Where are your gods that you made for yourself? Will they rise and save you in the time of your affliction? For your gods were as numerous as your cities, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s streets they sacrificed to Baal.

targets.text: And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.

triples.relationship: parallel failure to respond to repeated divine discipline
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says blows upon the children were vain because discipline was not accepted. Amos repeatedly recounts blows, sword and destruction followed by failure to turn to God, matching the indictment of unresponsive recipients without equating every punishment.

source.text: In vain I struck your children; you accepted no discipline. A sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion, and you did not fear.
source.display_text: In vain I struck your children; you accepted no discipline. A sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion, and you did not fear.

targets.text: “I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
targets.display_text: “I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

targets.text: “I sent death among you on Egypt’s road and killed your young men with the sword, along with the captivity of your horses. I brought your camps up in fire in My anger; yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
targets.display_text: “I sent death among you on Egypt’s road and killed your young men with the sword, along with the captivity of your horses. I brought your camps up in fire in My anger; yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

targets.text: “I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
targets.display_text: “I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

triples.relationship: related indictment of rejecting the God who sustained Israel
triples.rationale: God asks whether He became a wilderness or barren land to Israel while the people reject His rule. Deuteronomy describes the nourished and satisfied people forsaking their Maker and forgetting the God who nourishes them, supplying the corresponding contrast between divine provision and rejection.

source.text: Hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to Israel, or a land left barren? Why did My people say, We will not be ruled, and we will come to Thee no more?
source.display_text: Hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to Israel, or a land left barren? Why did My people say, We will not be ruled, and we will come to Thee no more?

targets.text: And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; and he forsook God who made him, and departed from God his Saviour.
They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.
You forsook God who begat you, and forgot God who nourishes you.

triples.relationship: contrast between the people's forgetfulness and God's refusal to forget
triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares the people's long forgetfulness of God with the implausibility of a bride or virgin forgetting adornment. Isaiah answers Zion's complaint of being forgotten with God's refusal to forget her; the direction of the forgetting is reversed.

source.text: Will a bride forget her adornment, or a virgin her breastband? Yet My people forgot Me for days beyond counting.
source.display_text: Will a bride forget her adornment, or a virgin her breastband? Yet My people forgot Me for days beyond counting.

targets.text: But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
targets.display_text: But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”

targets.text: “Will a woman forget her child, failing to have mercy on the offspring of her belly? Even if a woman forgets these, I will not forget you,” said the Lord.
targets.display_text: “Will a woman forget her child, failing to have mercy on the offspring of her belly? Even if a woman forgets these, I will not forget you,” said the Lord.

targets.text: “Behold, on My hands I painted your walls, and you are before Me continually.
targets.display_text: “Behold, on My hands I painted your walls, and you are before Me continually.

triples.relationship: legal contrast distinguishing innocent blood from a fatal break-in
triples.rationale: Jeremiah charges bloodshed against innocent lives and explicitly says they were not found in break-ins. Exodus excludes murder in the death of a thief found breaking in and then distinguishes a case after sunrise; this supplies a legal contrast without resolving the target's later pronouns or Jeremiah's oak detail.

source.text: Even on your hands was found the blood of innocent lives. I did not find them in break-ins, but at every oak.
source.display_text: Even on your hands was found the blood of innocent lives. I did not find them in break-ins, but at every oak.

targets.text: “And if the thief is found breaking in, and is struck and dies, there is no murder in his case.
But if the sun has risen upon him, he is guilty; he shall die in return. And if he has nothing, let him be sold for the theft.

triples.relationship: parallel rejection of a claim to have no sin
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces judgment precisely because the people say they did not sin. First John likewise rejects claims of having no sin or not having sinned and contrasts them with confession and cleansing.

source.text: And you said, I am innocent; let His fury turn away from me. Behold, I enter judgment with you because you say, I did not sin.
source.display_text: And you said, I am innocent; let His fury turn away from me. Behold, I enter judgment with you because you say, I did not sin.

targets.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
targets.display_text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

targets.text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
targets.display_text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

targets.text: If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us.
targets.display_text: If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us.

triples.relationship: parallel shame resulting from reliance on Egypt
triples.rationale: Jeremiah predicts that Egypt will put the people to shame as Assyria did. Isaiah likewise says Pharaoh's shelter and the hoped-for Egyptian assistance will become shame and reproach rather than benefit.

source.text: Why did you show such contempt by repeating your ways? You will also be put to shame by Egypt, as you were put to shame by Assyria.
source.display_text: Why did you show such contempt by repeating your ways? You will also be put to shame by Egypt, as you were put to shame by Assyria.

targets.text: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
targets.display_text: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.

targets.text: For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain
targets.display_text: For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain

targets.text: toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”
targets.display_text: toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”

triples.relationship: shared gesture of departing with hands on the head
triples.rationale: Jeremiah predicts departure with hands upon the head after the Lord rejects the people's hope. Tamar likewise leaves with her hands on her head and cries out; the visible gesture is shared, while her victimization must not be treated as the same moral situation as Judah's judgment.

source.text: For from here too you will go out with your hands on your head, because the Lord rejected your hope, and you will not prosper in it.
source.display_text: For from here too you will go out with your hands on your head, because the Lord rejected your hope, and you will not prosper in it.

targets.text: Tamar took ashes and put them on her head and tore the tunic with sleeves reaching the wrists that she was wearing. She put her hands on her head and went away, crying out as she went.
targets.display_text: Tamar took ashes and put them on her head and tore the tunic with sleeves reaching the wrists that she was wearing. She put her hands on her head and went away, crying out as she went.

triples.relationship: legal background to the divorce and remarriage question
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks whether a dismissed wife who becomes another man's will return to her former husband, before confronting the people's many shepherds. Deuteronomy forbids the former husband from taking such a wife back after the intervening marriage, supplying the stated legal analogy rather than resolving all the prophetic question's implications.

source.text: If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s, surely she will not return to him again? Would not that woman be utterly polluted? And you prostituted yourself with many shepherds—and were you returning to Me? says the Lord.
source.display_text: If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s, surely she will not return to him again? Would not that woman be utterly polluted? And you prostituted yourself with many shepherds—and were you returning to Me? says the Lord.

triples.relationship: parallel roadside prostitution imagery for covenant infidelity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah portrays the woman seated on roads and polluting the land through prostitution. Ezekiel's address to Jerusalem describes prostitution chambers in broad streets and at road heads, giving a particular counterpart to the public locations without reproducing the solitary-crow image.

targets.text: and at the head of every road you built your brothels, ruined your beauty, spread your legs to every passerby, and multiplied your prostitution.

targets.text: You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.
targets.display_text: You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

triples.relationship: parallel prostitute appearance and shameless face
triples.rationale: Jeremiah charges the people with a prostitute's appearance and shamelessness. Proverbs describes the seductress with a prostitute's appearance and a shameless face; Jeremiah applies such language collectively rather than narrating the same individual encounter.

source.display_text: You had many shepherds as a stumbling block for yourself. You had a prostitute’s appearance; you were shameless toward everyone.

targets.display_text: She is fluttering with excitement and dissolute; her feet do not rest in the house.

targets.display_text: For at one time she roams outside, and at another she lies in wait in the squares, at every corner.

triples.relationship: related appeal to divine fatherhood amid covenant infidelity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah recalls calling God a father and leader of virginity amid accusations of faithlessness. Malachi asks whether all have one Father and then indicts covenant profanation and devotion to foreign gods, likewise exposing a gap between the paternal relationship and conduct.

source.text: Did you not call Me a household, a father and the leader of your virginity?
source.display_text: Did you not call Me a household, a father and the leader of your virginity?

targets.text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?
targets.display_text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?

targets.text: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the Lord’s holy things, in which he delighted, and devoted himself to foreign gods.
targets.display_text: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the Lord’s holy things, in which he delighted, and devoted himself to foreign gods.

triples.relationship: parallel prostitution imagery linked with hilltop and tree-shaded worship
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes Israel's prostitution on high mountains and beneath wooded trees. Hosea similarly joins a spirit of prostitution and departure from God with sacrifices on mountaintops, hills and beneath named shade trees.

source.text: The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.
source.display_text: The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.

targets.text: They inquired by signs, and by his rods they announced things to him; they were led astray by a spirit of prostitution and prostituted themselves away from their God.
targets.display_text: They inquired by signs, and by his rods they announced things to him; they were led astray by a spirit of prostitution and prostituted themselves away from their God.

targets.text: On the mountaintops they sacrificed, and on the hills they offered sacrifice, beneath oak, poplar and a tree providing shade, because shelter is good. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
targets.display_text: On the mountaintops they sacrificed, and on the hills they offered sacrifice, beneath oak, poplar and a tree providing shade, because shelter is good. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

triples.relationship: parallel divine summons met by departure rather than return
triples.rationale: God calls Israel to return, but she does not. Hosea likewise recalls God's summons followed by departure from His presence and sacrifice to Baalim; Jeremiah additionally says Judah observed Israel's faithlessness.

source.text: After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.
source.display_text: After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.

targets.text: Because Israel was an infant, I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned his children.
targets.display_text: Because Israel was an infant, I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned his children.

targets.text: As I summoned them, so they departed from My presence; they sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved images.
targets.display_text: As I summoned them, so they departed from My presence; they sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved images.

triples.relationship: related divorce-document imagery for separation caused by unfaithfulness
triples.rationale: Jeremiah explicitly says God sent Israel away and gave her a divorce certificate. Isaiah asks about the mother's divorce document and attributes her dismissal to lawless acts; the rhetorical question and Jeremiah's explicit giving of a document are kept distinct.

source.text: I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
source.display_text: I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.

targets.text: Thus says the Lord: “What is your mother’s divorce document with which I sent her away? Or to which debtor have I sold you? Behold, you were sold because of your sins, and I sent your mother away because of your lawless acts.
targets.display_text: Thus says the Lord: “What is your mother’s divorce document with which I sent her away? Or to which debtor have I sold you? Behold, you were sold because of your sins, and I sent your mother away because of your lawless acts.

triples.relationship: parallel association of adultery imagery with idolatry
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes adultery with wood and stone. Ezekiel combines adultery with reflections, child offerings and the explicit mention of idols, placing false worship within the same language of marital unfaithfulness without replacing the target's unusual wording.

source.text: Her prostitution came to be regarded as nothing, and she committed adultery with wood and stone.
source.display_text: Her prostitution came to be regarded as nothing, and she committed adultery with wood and stone.

targets.text: for they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their reflections, and made their children whom they bore to Me pass through fire offerings for them.
targets.display_text: for they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their reflections, and made their children whom they bore to Me pass through fire offerings for them.

targets.text: They even did these things to Me: they defiled My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.
targets.display_text: They even did these things to Me: they defiled My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.

targets.text: When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My holy places to profane them. Indeed, they acted this way within My house.
targets.display_text: When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My holy places to profane them. Indeed, they acted this way within My house.

triples.relationship: parallel contrast between outward religious approach and a distant heart
triples.rationale: Judah's return is described as false rather than wholehearted. Isaiah similarly contrasts honoring God with lips and a heart far from Him, providing a precise counterpart to outward response lacking inward fidelity.

source.text: In all these things faithless Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood.
source.display_text: In all these things faithless Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood.

targets.text: The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.
targets.display_text: The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.

triples.relationship: parallel relative justification through another community's greater wrongdoing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says Israel is justified in comparison with faithless Judah. Ezekiel says Jerusalem's greater lawlessness justified her sisters, including Samaria; neither comparison declares the less guilty community absolutely innocent.

source.text: The Lord said to me, Israel has justified himself in comparison with faithless Judah.
source.display_text: The Lord said to me, Israel has justified himself in comparison with faithless Judah.

targets.text: Samaria did not sin half your sins. You multiplied your lawlessness beyond theirs and justified your sisters by all the lawlessness you committed.
targets.display_text: Samaria did not sin half your sins. You multiplied your lawlessness beyond theirs and justified your sisters by all the lawlessness you committed.

targets.text: You too, receive your torment, in which you corrupted your sisters by your sins, in which you acted more lawlessly than they and justified them above yourself. You too, be ashamed and take your dishonor, in that you justified your sisters.
targets.display_text: You too, receive your torment, in which you corrupted your sisters by your sins, in which you acted more lawlessly than they and justified them above yourself. You too, be ashamed and take your dishonor, in that you justified your sisters.

triples.relationship: parallel divine mercy and anger that does not last forever
triples.rationale: God invites Israel to return because He is merciful and will not remain angry forever. The psalm likewise calls Him compassionate and merciful and says He does not maintain wrath forever.

source.text: Go and read these words toward the north: Return to Me, dwelling of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set My face firmly against you, because I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.
source.display_text: Go and read these words toward the north: Return to Me, dwelling of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set My face firmly against you, because I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.

targets.text: The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.

targets.text: He will not be angry to the end, nor maintain wrath for ever.
targets.display_text:

triples.relationship: parallel acknowledgment of wrongdoing as the proper response
triples.rationale: Jeremiah demands recognition of injustice, disobedience and departure toward strangers. First John describes confession of sins together with divine forgiveness and cleansing; the shared response is acknowledgment rather than a denial of wrongdoing.

source.text: Only recognize your injustice: you acted ungodly toward the Lord your God and spread your ways to strangers beneath every wooded tree, but you did not obey My voice, says the Lord.
source.display_text: Only recognize your injustice: you acted ungodly toward the Lord your God and spread your ways to strangers beneath every wooded tree, but you did not obey My voice, says the Lord.

targets.text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
targets.display_text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

triples.relationship: parallel gathering of a scattered remnant
triples.rationale: God promises to take small numbers from cities and clans and bring them to Zion. Isaiah likewise promises recovery of a remaining remnant and the gathering of Israel's lost and Judah's scattered people, with a wider geographical enumeration rather than Jeremiah's numerical expressions.

source.text: Return, children who have withdrawn, says the Lord, because I will rule over you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you into Zion,
source.display_text: Return, children who have withdrawn, says the Lord, because I will rule over you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you into Zion,

targets.text: On that day the Lord will again show His hand, to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people left from the Assyrians, Egypt, Babylonia, Ethiopia, the Elamites, the sun’s rising and Arabia.
targets.display_text: On that day the Lord will again show His hand, to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people left from the Assyrians, Egypt, Babylonia, Ethiopia, the Elamites, the sun’s rising and Arabia.

targets.text: He will raise a signal to the nations and gather Israel’s lost ones; He will gather Judah’s scattered ones from the earth’s four wings.
targets.display_text: He will raise a signal to the nations and gather Israel’s lost ones; He will gather Judah’s scattered ones from the earth’s four wings.

triples.relationship: parallel divine provision of shepherds for the restored people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah promises shepherds according to God's heart who shepherd with knowledge. Ezekiel promises one shepherd, God's servant David, over the people; the divine provision is common, while the plural shepherds and the single named shepherd are distinct.

source.text: and I will give you shepherds according to My heart, and they will shepherd you, shepherding with knowledge.
source.display_text: and I will give you shepherds according to My heart, and they will shepherd you, shepherding with knowledge.

targets.text: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.
targets.display_text: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.

targets.text: I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
targets.display_text: I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.

triples.relationship: parallel future gathering of nations to Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says Jerusalem will be called the Lord's throne and nations will gather there. Isaiah likewise describes nations coming to the Lord's mountain and receiving His way, with law and the Lord's word proceeding from Zion and Jerusalem.

source.text: In those days and at that time they will call Jerusalem the Lord’s throne, and all the nations will gather to her. They will no longer follow the thoughts of their evil heart.
source.display_text: In those days and at that time they will call Jerusalem the Lord’s throne, and all the nations will gather to her. They will no longer follow the thoughts of their evil heart.

targets.text: In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

targets.text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.
targets.display_text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: parallel reunion of divided Israel in the inherited land
triples.rationale: Jeremiah promises that Judah will join Israel and return together from northern and other regions. Ezekiel promises gathering into Israel's land and an end to division into two nations or kingdoms, giving a corresponding account of reunion.

source.text: In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the northern land and from all the regions to the land I gave their fathers as an inheritance.
source.display_text: In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the northern land and from all the regions to the land I gave their fathers as an inheritance.

targets.display_text: My servant David will be ruler among them, and one shepherd will be over all, because they will walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.

triples.relationship: parallel acknowledgment of God as Father in relation to inheritance
triples.rationale: Jeremiah anticipates the people calling God Father and receiving a chosen inheritance. Isaiah's prayer calls the Lord Father and appeals concerning the tribes of His inheritance and the holy mountain; its petition differs from Jeremiah's promise.

source.text: And I said, May it be, Lord! For I will place you among children and give you a chosen land, an inheritance of God Almighty of nations. I said, You will call Me Father and will not turn away from Me.
source.display_text: And I said, May it be, Lord! For I will place you among children and give you a chosen land, an inheritance of God Almighty of nations. I said, You will call Me Father and will not turn away from Me.

targets.text: For Thou art our Father, because Abraham did not know us and Israel did not recognize us. But Thou, Lord, art our Father. Rescue us! From the beginning Thy name has been upon us.
targets.display_text: For Thou art our Father, because Abraham did not know us and Israel did not recognize us. But Thou, Lord, art our Father. Rescue us! From the beginning Thy name has been upon us.

targets.text: Why, Lord, didst Thou make us stray from Thy way and harden our hearts so that we do not fear Thee? Return because of Thy servants, because of the tribes of Thine inheritance,
targets.display_text: Why, Lord, didst Thou make us stray from Thy way and harden our hearts so that we do not fear Thee? Return because of Thy servants, because of the tribes of Thine inheritance,

targets.text: so that we may inherit a little of Thy holy mountain. Our adversaries trampled Thy sanctuary.
targets.display_text: so that we may inherit a little of Thy holy mountain. Our adversaries trampled Thy sanctuary.

triples.relationship: parallel portrayal of the people's infidelity through a broken marriage
triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares Israel's faithlessness with a woman's faithlessness toward her partner. Hosea likewise portrays the mother through prostitution and the repudiated wife-husband relationship, using marital language for the people's departure.

source.text: But as a woman deals faithlessly with the one living with her, so the house of Israel dealt faithlessly with Me, says the Lord.
source.display_text: But as a woman deals faithlessly with the one living with her, so the house of Israel dealt faithlessly with Me, says the Lord.

targets.text: “Enter into judgment with your mother, enter into judgment! For she is not My wife and I am not her husband. I will remove her prostitution from My face and her adultery from between her breasts,

targets.display_text: For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’

triples.relationship: parallel weeping associated with returning from wrongdoing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah hears the weeping and supplication of Israel's children after their unjust ways and forgetting God. Joel calls for return to God with weeping, mourning and a torn heart, giving the corresponding summons to penitential sorrow.

source.text: A voice was heard from lips, the weeping and supplication of Israel’s children, because they acted unjustly in their ways and forgot their holy God.
source.display_text: A voice was heard from lips, the weeping and supplication of Israel’s children, because they acted unjustly in their ways and forgot their holy God.

targets.text: “And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
targets.display_text: “And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”

targets.display_text: Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.

triples.relationship: parallel summons to return followed by a promise of healing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah calls the returning children back and promises to heal their fractures. Hosea calls Israel to return with words and later promises to heal their dwellings; the return-and-healing pattern is shared while fractures and dwellings remain different expressions.

source.text: Return, returning children, and I will heal your fractures. Behold, we will be Thy servants, because Thou art the Lord our God.
source.display_text: Return, returning children, and I will heal your fractures. Behold, we will be Thy servants, because Thou art the Lord our God.

targets.display_text: Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Speak to Him so that you do not receive injustice but receive good things, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.

targets.display_text: Assur will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse, and we will certainly no longer call the works of our hands “Our gods.” The One in you will have mercy on an orphan.

targets.text: I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
targets.display_text: I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.

triples.relationship: related contrast between looking toward mountains and finding help in God
triples.rationale: Jeremiah declares the hills and the mountains' power false and locates Israel's salvation in the Lord. The psalm looks toward the mountains, asks where help comes from and answers that it comes from the Lord; it does not itself call the mountains false.

source.text: Truly the hills and the power of the mountains were false; but through the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.
source.display_text: Truly the hills and the power of the mountains were false; but through the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.

triples.relationship: parallel loss of livestock, children and the fruit of labor
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says shame consumed the fathers' labors, sheep, calves, sons and daughters. Deuteronomy's curse similarly describes livestock and children given away and an unknown nation consuming the people's labor; it supplies a concrete loss pattern without identifying Jeremiah's personified shame as that nation.

source.text: Shame consumed our fathers’ labors from our youth: their sheep and calves, their sons and daughters.
source.display_text: Shame consumed our fathers’ labors from our youth: their sheep and calves, their sons and daughters.

targets.text: Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.

A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.

triples.relationship: parallel corporate confession of longstanding sin and shame
triples.rationale: Jeremiah's speakers lie in shame and confess that they and their fathers sinned from youth to the present. Ezra likewise confesses accumulated lawlessness from the fathers' days to the present and speaks of shame before God.

source.text: We lay down in our shame, and our dishonor covered us, because we sinned before our God, we and our fathers, from our youth until this day, and did not obey the voice of the Lord our God.
source.display_text: We lay down in our shame, and our dishonor covered us, because we sinned before our God, we and our fathers, from our youth until this day, and did not obey the voice of the Lord our God.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah conditions Israel's return on removing abominations from the mouth and reverence before God. Hosea similarly calls Israel to return with words and renounce calling human handiwork gods, joining verbal response with rejection of false worship.
