triples.relationship: parallel demand for truth, just judgment and truthful oaths
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes swearing that the Lord lives with truth, judgment and righteousness. Zechariah likewise commands truth and peaceful judgment while rejecting love of a false oath; Jeremiah additionally anticipates blessing among nations.

source.text: and swears, ‘The Lord lives,’ with truth and in judgment and righteousness, then nations will bless in her, and in Him they will praise God in Jerusalem.
source.display_text: and swears, ‘The Lord lives,’ with truth and in judgment and righteousness, then nations will bless in her, and in Him they will praise God in Jerusalem.

targets.text: These are the things you shall do: speak truth, each to his neighbor, and render peaceful judgment in your gates.
targets.display_text: These are the things you shall do: speak truth, each to his neighbor, and render peaceful judgment in your gates.

targets.text: Do not reckon your neighbor’s wrong in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.”
targets.display_text: Do not reckon your neighbor’s wrong in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.”

triples.relationship: related cultivation imagery for a righteous response to God
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands breaking fallow ground and avoiding sowing among thorns. Hosea commands sowing in righteousness, reaping life's fruit and seeking the Lord; its supplied wording does not repeat the fallow-ground command, but both frame the needed response through cultivation.

source.text: For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Break up fallow ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.
source.display_text: For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Break up fallow ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.

targets.text: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap life’s fruit. Shine a light of knowledge for yourselves; seek the Lord until produce of righteousness comes to you.
targets.display_text: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap life’s fruit. Shine a light of knowledge for yourselves; seek the Lord until produce of righteousness comes to you.

triples.relationship: repeated command to circumcise hardness of heart
triples.rationale: Jeremiah calls Judah and Jerusalem to circumcise their hardness of heart. Deuteronomy gives the same inward command and adds that they must no longer stiffen their neck, clarifying the obedience sought through the image.

source.text: Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.
source.display_text: Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.

targets.text: And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.

triples.relationship: related interpretation of circumcision as an inward matter
triples.rationale: Jeremiah directs circumcision toward hardness of heart rather than merely a physical act. Romans likewise speaks of circumcision of the heart in Spirit and inward identity; its argument about who is a Jew is not explicitly stated in Jeremiah's warning.

source.text: Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.
source.display_text: Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.

targets.text: For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;
targets.display_text: For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;

targets.text: but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.
targets.display_text: but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

triples.relationship: parallel trumpet alarm addressed to Zion's region
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands a trumpet signal and loud warning in Judah and Jerusalem as people gather toward walled cities. Joel similarly commands the trumpet in Zion and proclamation on the holy mountain, explaining the alarm through the announced Lord's day.

source.text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
source.display_text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!

targets.text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,
targets.display_text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,

triples.relationship: repeated warning of northern evils and great crushing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah urges flight to Zion because evils and great crushing are coming from the north. Jeremiah 6 repeats the northern direction and great crushing while addressing Benjamin and calling for warning signals.

source.text: Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
source.display_text: Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.

targets.text: Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,
targets.display_text: Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,

triples.relationship: parallel lion imagery producing desolated land and empty cities
triples.rationale: The departing lion destroys nations and leaves the land desolate and cities without inhabitants. Jeremiah 2 likewise joins roaring lions with wilderness and demolished, uninhabited cities, giving a close earlier form of the same destructive imagery.

source.text: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.
source.display_text: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.

targets.text: Lions roared over him and raised their voice. They made his land a wilderness, and his cities were demolished so that none inhabited them.
targets.display_text: Lions roared over him and raised their voice. They made his land a wilderness, and his cities were demolished so that none inhabited them.

triples.relationship: parallel summons to sackcloth and lament under divine calamity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands sackcloth, mourning and wailing because the Lord's fury has not turned away. Joel likewise summons ministers to lament and sleep in sackcloth, then announces the near day of the Lord; the addressees and immediate reasons differ.

source.text: For these things, gird yourselves with sackcloth, beat yourselves in mourning and wail, because the Lord’s fury has not turned away from you.
source.display_text: For these things, gird yourselves with sackcloth, beat yourselves in mourning and wail, because the Lord’s fury has not turned away from you.

targets.text: Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
targets.display_text: Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.

targets.text: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,
targets.display_text: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,

targets.text: “Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”
targets.display_text: “Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”

triples.relationship: parallel collapse of civil and religious leadership during judgment
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes the failure of kings and rulers and the astonishment of priests and prophets. Ezekiel likewise depicts the loss of priestly law and elders' counsel, a sought prophetic vision and a ruler clothed in devastation, showing institutions overwhelmed by judgment.

source.text: And it will be on that day, says the Lord: the king’s heart and the rulers’ heart will perish, and the priests will be beside themselves and the prophets astonished.
source.display_text: And it will be on that day, says the Lord: the king’s heart and the rulers’ heart will perish, and the priests will be beside themselves and the prophets astonished.

targets.text: Woe upon woe will come, and message upon message; a vision will be sought from a prophet, but law will perish from a priest and counsel from elders.
targets.display_text: Woe upon woe will come, and message upon message; a vision will be sought from a prophet, but law will perish from a priest and counsel from elders.

targets.text: A ruler will clothe himself in devastation, and the hands of the people of the land will be paralyzed. According to their ways I will deal with them, and by their judgments I will exact retribution upon them; they will know that I am the Lord.’”
targets.display_text: A ruler will clothe himself in devastation, and the hands of the people of the land will be paralyzed. According to their ways I will deal with them, and by their judgments I will exact retribution upon them; they will know that I am the Lord.’”

triples.relationship: parallel exposure of proclaimed peace contradicted by reality
triples.rationale: Jeremiah protests that a promise of peace is contradicted by a sword reaching the people's soul. Jeremiah 6 likewise exposes the claim of peace by asking where peace is; that later charge against those treating the fracture does not settle every question about Jeremiah's address to God here.

source.text: And I said: O Master, Lord, surely Thou hast indeed deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ and behold, the sword has reached to their soul!
source.display_text: And I said: O Master, Lord, surely Thou hast indeed deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ and behold, the sword has reached to their soul!

targets.text: And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?
targets.display_text: And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

triples.relationship: parallel rapid invading cavalry compared with an eagle
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes stormlike chariots and horses swifter than eagles. Habakkuk's Chaldean warriors likewise rush from afar with horsemen flying like an eagle, using the bird's speed to depict invasion while retaining distinct animal comparisons.

source.text: Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!
source.display_text: Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!

targets.text: For look, I am raising up against you the Chaldean warriors, the bitter and swift nation, who traverse the breadth of the earth to possess dwellings not their own.
targets.display_text: For look, I am raising up against you the Chaldean warriors, the bitter and swift nation, who traverse the breadth of the earth to possess dwellings not their own.

targets.text: Fearsome and conspicuous are they; their judgment will come from themselves, and their claim will proceed from themselves.
targets.display_text: Fearsome and conspicuous are they; their judgment will come from themselves, and their claim will proceed from themselves.

targets.text: Their horses will leap beyond leopards and be fiercer than the wolves of Arabia. Their horsemen will ride out and rush from afar, flying like an eagle eager to eat.
targets.display_text: Their horses will leap beyond leopards and be fiercer than the wolves of Arabia. Their horsemen will ride out and rush from afar, flying like an eagle eager to eat.

triples.relationship: parallel command to wash away moral evil
triples.rationale: Jeremiah orders Jerusalem to wash its heart of evil rather than retain harmful schemes. Isaiah likewise commands washing, removal of evils from souls and cessation of evil deeds, making the cleansing explicitly moral.

source.text: Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?
source.display_text: Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?

targets.text: Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
targets.display_text: Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

targets.text: Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
targets.display_text: Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.

triples.relationship: repeated northern warning associated with Dan
triples.rationale: Jeremiah anticipates an announcing voice from Dan and trouble from Ephraim. Jeremiah 8 again locates an alarming sound at Dan, this time the horses of an approaching destroyer; the source's announcement and the target's cavalry sound remain distinct.

source.text: For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.
source.display_text: For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.

targets.text: From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.
targets.display_text: From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.

triples.relationship: parallel threat from distant forces
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces bands from a distant land raising their voice against Judah's cities. Isaiah likewise describes a signal among distant nations and their rapid, armed arrival, giving the military counterpart to the distant bands.

source.text: Remind the nations: Behold, they have come! Announce in Jerusalem: Bands come from a distant land and have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.
source.display_text: Remind the nations: Behold, they have come! Announce in Jerusalem: Bands come from a distant land and have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.

targets.text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!
targets.display_text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!

targets.text: They will not hunger or grow weary, slumber or sleep, nor loosen the belts from their waists; their sandal straps will certainly not break.
targets.display_text: They will not hunger or grow weary, slumber or sleep, nor loosen the belts from their waists; their sandal straps will certainly not break.

targets.text: Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.
targets.display_text: Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.

targets.text: They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.
targets.display_text: They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.

triples.relationship: parallel encirclement of Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares the forces around the city to those guarding a field. Jeremiah 6 depicts shepherds and flocks pitching tents against Zion all around, repeating the surrounding position through a different rural image.

source.text: Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.
source.display_text: Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.

targets.text: Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will shepherd with his own hand.
targets.display_text: Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will shepherd with his own hand.

triples.relationship: repeated explanation that the people's own evil brings bitter consequences
triples.rationale: Jeremiah attributes what happened to the people's ways and practices and calls the result bitter. Jeremiah 2 similarly says apostasy and evil will discipline and rebuke them and describes abandonment of God as bitter.

source.text: Your ways and your practices have done these things to you. This is your evil: it is bitter; it has reached to your heart.
source.display_text: Your ways and your practices have done these things to you. This is your evil: it is bitter; it has reached to your heart.

targets.text: Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.
targets.display_text: Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

triples.relationship: parallel bodily pain and a troubled heart amid an ominous message
triples.rationale: Jeremiah speaks of pain in the belly, a torn heart and the heard cry of war. Isaiah's speaker likewise describes a harsh vision, bodily weakness, labor pains and a wandering, fearful heart; the particular vision and Jeremiah's trumpet report are distinct.

source.text: My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.
source.display_text: My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.

targets.text: and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
targets.display_text: and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.

targets.text: Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.
targets.display_text: Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.

targets.text: My heart wanders, and lawlessness submerges me; my soul stands in fear.
targets.display_text: My heart wanders, and lawlessness submerges me; my soul stands in fear.

triples.relationship: repeated lament over a ruined tent and torn coverings
triples.rationale: Jeremiah laments sudden misery affecting the tent and torn coverings. Jeremiah 10 again describes the tent's misery and destruction and all its coverings torn, then adds the loss of sons and sheep.

source.text: It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.
source.display_text: It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.

targets.text: My tent suffered misery and perished, and all my tent coverings were torn apart. My sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my coverings.
targets.display_text: My tent suffered misery and perished, and all my tent coverings were torn apart. My sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my coverings.

triples.relationship: same-chapter recurrence of the trumpet heard in distress
triples.rationale: The question about how long flight and trumpet sounds will continue resumes the earlier voice's distress at a trumpet and cry of war. The explicit repeated sound connects the lamenting question with the preceding bodily anguish.

source.text: How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?
source.display_text: How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?

targets.text: My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.
targets.display_text: My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.

triples.relationship: contrast between skill in evil and wisdom in goodness
triples.rationale: Jeremiah calls the leaders of the people wise at evil but untrained in doing good. Paul desires the opposite orientation: wisdom about good and innocence about evil, furnishing a sharply reversed moral pattern.

source.text: For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.
source.display_text: For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.

targets.text: For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
targets.display_text: For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

triples.relationship: literary contrast with the appearance of earth and light in creation
triples.rationale: Jeremiah looks at earth and sees nothing, and finds heaven's lights absent. Genesis moves from the unseen, unformed earth and darkness to God's creation of light; the comparison reads Jeremiah's desolation against creation without substituting Genesis's wording for Jeremiah's.

source.text: I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.
source.display_text: I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.

targets.text: In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
Now the earth was unseen and unformed, and darkness was over the deep; and the Spirit of God was moving over the water.
And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
And God saw that the light was good, and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning: one day.

triples.relationship: parallel trembling of mountains and hills before divine wrath
triples.rationale: Jeremiah sees mountains trembling and hills shaken in a scene explained through the Lord's anger. Nahum likewise describes mountains and hills shaking before Him and asks who can resist His furious wrath.

source.text: I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were being shaken.
source.display_text: I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were being shaken.

targets.text: Mountains shook before Him and hills were shaken; the whole earth recoiled before Him, and all who dwell in it.
targets.display_text: Mountains shook before Him and hills were shaken; the whole earth recoiled before Him, and all who dwell in it.

targets.text: Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.
targets.display_text: Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

triples.relationship: contrast with creation's birds and humanity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah's vision contains no human and birds of heaven in terror. Genesis describes the making and blessing of birds and the making of humanity; human absence and frightened birds invert the ordered, populated creation without saying Jeremiah's birds are absent.

source.text: I looked, and behold, there was no human, and all the birds of heaven were terrified.
source.display_text: I looked, and behold, there was no human, and all the birds of heaven were terrified.

targets.text: And God said, “Let the waters bring forth living creatures that move, and birds that fly above the earth across the firmament of heaven.” And it was so.

And God made the great sea creatures, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that they were good.
And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas; and let the birds multiply upon the earth.”
And there was evening, and there was morning: a fifth day.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: four-footed animals, creeping things, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so.

And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.

And God said, “Let Us make man in Our image and likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

triples.relationship: parallel change of Carmel or Chermel into wilderness
triples.rationale: Jeremiah sees Carmel become wilderness amid burned cities. Isaiah's supplied text likewise says Chermel will become wilderness after describing abandoned houses and a deserted city, providing the same direction of change with a different form of the place-name.

source.text: I saw, and behold, Carmel was a wilderness, and all the cities were burned with fire before the Lord, and they vanished before His furious anger.
source.display_text: I saw, and behold, Carmel was a wilderness, and all the cities were burned with fire before the Lord, and they vanished before His furious anger.

targets.text: My people’s earth will grow thorn and grass, and joy will be removed from every house. Wealthy city,
targets.display_text: My people’s earth will grow thorn and grass, and joy will be removed from every house. Wealthy city,

targets.text: houses abandoned! They will leave the city’s wealth and desirable houses; villages will become caves for ever, wild donkeys’ delight, pastures for shepherds,
targets.display_text: houses abandoned! They will leave the city’s wealth and desirable houses; villages will become caves for ever, wild donkeys’ delight, pastures for shepherds,

targets.text: until a spirit from on high comes upon you. Chermel will become wilderness, and Chermel will be reckoned as forest.
targets.display_text: until a spirit from on high comes upon you. Chermel will become wilderness, and Chermel will be reckoned as forest.

triples.relationship: repeated limit on destruction: no complete end
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces wilderness for the land but expressly excludes a complete end. Jeremiah 5 repeats God's promise not to bring the people to a complete end amid the invasion warnings.

source.text: Thus says the Lord: The whole land will be a wilderness, but I will certainly not make a complete end.
source.display_text: Thus says the Lord: The whole land will be a wilderness, but I will certainly not make a complete end.

targets.text: And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.
targets.display_text: And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.

triples.relationship: parallel declaration that God's announced purpose will not be reversed
triples.rationale: Jeremiah explains mourning and darkened heaven by God's settled speech and refusal to turn back. Isaiah likewise says what God spoke and counseled will stand and asks who can turn back His hand, though that oracle specifically concerns Assyria.

source.text: For these things let the earth mourn and let heaven above grow dark, because I have spoken and will not change My mind; I have set Myself in motion and will not turn back from it.
source.display_text: For these things let the earth mourn and let heaven above grow dark, because I have spoken and will not change My mind; I have set Myself in motion and will not turn back from it.

targets.text: Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “As I said, so it will be, and as I counseled, so it will endure,
targets.display_text: Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “As I said, so it will be, and as I counseled, so it will endure,

targets.text: to destroy the Assyrians from My land and from My mountains. They will become a trampling place; their yoke will be removed from them, and their glory removed from the shoulders.”
targets.display_text: to destroy the Assyrians from My land and from My mountains. They will become a trampling place; their yoke will be removed from them, and their glory removed from the shoulders.”

targets.text: This is the counsel the Lord has counseled concerning the whole inhabited world, and this the high hand over all the world’s nations.
targets.display_text: This is the counsel the Lord has counseled concerning the whole inhabited world, and this the high hand over all the world’s nations.

targets.text: For what the holy God has counseled, who will scatter? And who will turn back the high hand?
targets.display_text: For what the holy God has counseled, who will scatter? And who will turn back the high hand?

triples.relationship: parallel refuge in caves and rocks under overwhelming threat
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes flight into caves, groves and rocks at cavalry and bows. Isaiah likewise describes entry into rock clefts and holes before the Lord's terror; the refuges correspond while the stated immediate threats differ.

source.text: At the sound of a horseman and a drawn bow the whole countryside withdrew; they entered caves and hid in groves and climbed onto the rocks. Every city was abandoned; no human dwells in them.
source.display_text: At the sound of a horseman and a drawn bow the whole countryside withdrew; they entered caves and hid in groves and climbed onto the rocks. Every city was abandoned; no human dwells in them.

targets.text: carrying them into caves, into clefts in the rocks and into holes in the earth, from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
targets.display_text: carrying them into caves, into clefts in the rocks and into holes in the earth, from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.

targets.text: For on that day a person will cast out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to worship, to the worthless ones and the bats,
targets.display_text: For on that day a person will cast out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to worship, to the worthless ones and the bats,

targets.text: to enter holes in the solid rock and clefts in the rocks from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.

triples.relationship: parallel painted eyes and ornaments within a condemned lovers image

triples.rationale: Jeremiah hears Zion groaning like a woman giving birth for the first time and failing over the killed. Micah likewise addresses Zion through labor pains and a woman giving birth, adding exile and promised rescue rather than Jeremiah's particular lament over deaths.

triples.relationship: parallel mercy for a city conditional on finding righteous people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah calls for a search for even one person doing justice and seeking faithfulness, with mercy promised if found. Genesis likewise presents sparing Sodom for righteous inhabitants, with the requested numbers descending to ten rather than Jeremiah's one.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah 5 exposes falsehood beneath the oath that the Lord lives. Jeremiah 4 describes that same oath uttered with truth, judgment and righteousness, making the required quality of the oath explicit.

triples.relationship: parallel resistance to correction despite repeated punishment
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says the people refuse instruction and refuse to return even after scourging and devastation. Amos likewise recounts destructive blows and repeatedly says that the people still did not turn to God.

triples.relationship: same-chapter contrast between poor and prosperous people in disobedience
triples.rationale: The speaker first considers people who may be poor and lack ability and knowledge of God's way. triples.rationale: The prosperous people together break the yoke and tear bonds despite recognizing God's way. The psalm likewise portrays kings and rulers opposing the Lord and His anointed by proposing to tear bonds and cast off the yoke; the groups are not identical.

triples.relationship: parallel predatory animals in the judgment of Israel
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes lion, wolf and leopard attacks because of multiplied impieties. triples.relationship: commandment counterpart to desire for a neighbor's wife
triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares the people's desire for their neighbors' wives to horses mad for mares. Exodus explicitly prohibits coveting a neighbor's wife, supplying the command violated by the depicted desire.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces a nation from far away whose language Israel will not understand. Deuteronomy's curse likewise brings a distant nation whose speech is not understood, adding its merciless character.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah addresses a foolish people who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear. Isaiah's commission similarly describes hearing without understanding and seeing without perception, expanding the image through dull hearts and closed eyes.

triples.rationale: Jeremiah finds impious people setting traps to destroy and catch men. The psalm likewise asks rescue from unjust people who devise stumbling and hide traps and cords for the speaker's feet.

source.text: For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
source.display_text: For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.

targets.text: Guard me, Lord, from a sinner’s hand; rescue me from unjust people, those who devised to trip my steps.
The proud hid a trap for me and stretched cords, traps for my feet; along the path they set a stumbling block for me. Diapsalma.

triples.relationship: parallel enrichment of houses through predatory wrongdoing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah compares houses full of deceit with a bird-filled trap and connects this with wealth. Proverbs portrays violent people seeking to fill their houses with spoils and later mentions nets for birds, placing acquisitive violence and trapping imagery within one warning.

source.text: Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.
source.display_text: Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.

targets.text: Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
targets.display_text: Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.

targets.text: Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
targets.display_text: Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.

targets.text: Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
targets.display_text: Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,

targets.text: for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.
targets.display_text: for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.

targets.text: For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.
targets.display_text: For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.

targets.text: For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
targets.display_text: For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.

targets.text: These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
targets.display_text: These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.

triples.relationship: parallel denial of justice to orphans and widows
triples.rationale: Jeremiah charges failure to judge the orphan's and widow's cases. Isaiah similarly indicts rulers who do not judge for orphans or attend to widows' judgment, giving a close judicial counterpart.

source.text: And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.
source.display_text: And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.

targets.text: Your rulers disobey, partners of thieves, loving gifts and pursuing repayment, not judging for orphans and not attending to widows’ judgment.
targets.display_text: Your rulers disobey, partners of thieves, loving gifts and pursuing repayment, not judging for orphans and not attending to widows’ judgment.

triples.relationship: repeated visitation-and-vengeance refrain following social wrongdoing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks whether God will not visit and take vengeance after the account of predatory enrichment and failed justice. Jeremiah 9 repeats the two questions after deceit and concealed enmity, extending the same refrain to another social offense.

source.text: Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?
source.display_text: Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?

targets.text: Their tongue is a wounding missile; the utterances of their mouth are deceitful. One speaks peaceful things to his neighbor, and within himself he holds enmity.

targets.text: Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a people?
targets.display_text: Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a people?

triples.relationship: parallel public preference for false religious speech
triples.rationale: Jeremiah reports unjust prophecy, priestly applause and a people who love that arrangement. Second Timothy similarly predicts people preferring teachers suited to their desires and turning from truth to myths; it parallels the audience's complicity without identifying the later teachers with Jeremiah's prophets.

source.text: The prophets prophesy unjust things, and the priests applauded with their hands, and My people loved it so. And what will you do after these things?
source.display_text: The prophets prophesy unjust things, and the priests applauded with their hands, and My people loved it so. And what will you do after these things?

targets.text: For a time will come when they will not endure sound teaching, but with itching ears they will heap up teachers for themselves according to their own desires,
targets.display_text: For a time will come when they will not endure sound teaching, but with itching ears they will heap up teachers for themselves according to their own desires,

targets.text: and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
targets.display_text: and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn aside to myths.

triples.relationship: repeated trumpet warning of northern calamity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 6 calls for a trumpet in Tekoa and a sign above Beth-haccherem because of northern evils and crushing. Jeremiah 4 likewise joins a trumpet alarm with northern evils and great crushing, while directing flight toward Zion.

source.text: Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,
source.display_text: Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,

targets.text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
targets.display_text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!

targets.text: Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
targets.display_text: Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.

triples.relationship: parallel rural imagery for forces surrounding the city
triples.rationale: The shepherds and their flocks pitch tents against Zion all around. Jeremiah 4 likewise compares the encircling forces to those guarding a field, giving a corresponding rural image of military encirclement.

source.text: Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will shepherd with his own hand.
source.display_text: Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will shepherd with his own hand.

targets.text: Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.
targets.display_text: Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: same-chapter change from a proposed noon assault to a night assault
triples.rationale: The call to attack at noon is interrupted by the complaint that daylight has declined. The following call proposes rising in the night to destroy the foundations, specifically continuing the attack plan despite the change of time.

source.text: Prepare yourselves for war against her! Rise, and let us go up against her at noon! Woe to us, because the day has declined, because evening’s shadows are failing!
source.display_text: Prepare yourselves for war against her! Rise, and let us go up against her at noon! Woe to us, because the day has declined, because evening’s shadows are failing!

targets.text: Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!
targets.display_text: Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!

triples.relationship: parallel threat against city foundations
triples.rationale: Jeremiah's attacking voices propose destroying the city's foundations. Hosea likewise links Judah's multiplied walled cities and Israel's forgotten Maker with divine fire that devours city foundations; Hosea does not specify Jeremiah's night attack.

source.text: Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!
source.display_text: Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!

targets.text: Israel forgot his Maker, and they built sacred precincts; Judah multiplied walled cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.
targets.display_text: Israel forgot his Maker, and they built sacred precincts; Judah multiplied walled cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.

triples.relationship: legal counterpart to cutting trees during a siege
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands cutting the city's trees and pouring a force upon Jerusalem. Deuteronomy discusses cutting trees to build siegeworks and restricts the practice to trees without edible fruit; Jeremiah does not identify the tree types, so the link does not presume a violation of that restriction.

source.text: For thus says the Lord: Cut down her trees; pour out a force upon Jerusalem. O false city, all oppression is within her!
source.display_text: For thus says the Lord: Cut down her trees; pour out a force upon Jerusalem. O false city, all oppression is within her!

targets.text: And if you besiege a city many days, to fight against it and take it, you shall not destroy its trees by laying iron against them; for you may eat of them, and shall not cut them down. Is the tree of the field a man, that it should enter the siege before you?
But the tree which you know bears no fruit for food, you may destroy and cut down, and build siegeworks against the city which makes war with you, until it is delivered up.

triples.relationship: parallel discipline opposed to the city's destruction
triples.rationale: Jeremiah speaks of Jerusalem being instructed lest God's soul depart and it become uninhabitable. Zephaniah likewise indicts a city's refusal of discipline and reports a promise against destruction tied to fear of God and acceptance of discipline.

source.text: you will be instructed, Jerusalem, lest My soul depart from you, lest I make you an impassable land that will not be inhabited.
source.display_text: you will be instructed, Jerusalem, lest My soul depart from you, lest I make you an impassable land that will not be inhabited.

targets.text: She did not heed a voice or accept discipline; she did not trust the Lord or approach her God.
targets.display_text: She did not heed a voice or accept discipline; she did not trust the Lord or approach her God.

targets.text: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like Arabian wolves, leaving nothing for morning.
targets.display_text: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like Arabian wolves, leaving nothing for morning.

targets.text: Her prophets are bearers of a spirit, contemptuous men; her priests profane holy things and act impiously toward law.
targets.display_text: Her prophets are bearers of a spirit, contemptuous men; her priests profane holy things and act impiously toward law.

targets.text: But the Lord is righteous within her and will certainly do no injustice. Morning by morning He will bring His judgment to light; He was not hidden and knew no injustice in exaction, nor injustice in strife.
targets.display_text: But the Lord is righteous within her and will certainly do no injustice. Morning by morning He will bring His judgment to light; He was not hidden and knew no injustice in exaction, nor injustice in strife.

targets.text: In destruction I tore down the proud; their corners vanished. I will make their roads utterly desolate, with no passing through; their cities failed because no one existed or dwelt there.
targets.display_text: In destruction I tore down the proud; their corners vanished. I will make their roads utterly desolate, with no passing through; their cities failed because no one existed or dwelt there.

targets.text: I said, “Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will certainly not be destroyed from her eyes,” with all I exacted upon her. Prepare, rise early! All their gleaning has been ruined.
targets.display_text: I said, “Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will certainly not be destroyed from her eyes,” with all I exacted upon her. Prepare, rise early! All their gleaning has been ruined.

triples.relationship: related harvesting imagery for a diminished Israel
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands further gleaning of Israel's remnants as a vine is gleaned. Isaiah similarly portrays diminished Jacob through a gathered harvest, a remaining stalk and sparse olives; the source's further gleaning and the target's residual produce are related but distinct aspects of the image.

source.text: For thus says the Lord: Glean, glean Israel’s remnants like a vine; turn back like the grape-gatherer to his basket.
source.display_text: For thus says the Lord: Glean, glean Israel’s remnants like a vine; turn back like the grape-gatherer to his basket.

targets.text: On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.
targets.display_text: On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.

targets.text: It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,
targets.display_text: It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,

targets.text: and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.
targets.display_text: and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.

triples.relationship: parallel uncircumcised ears resistant to divine speech
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says uncircumcised ears cannot hear and refuse the Lord's utterance. Acts likewise addresses people as uncircumcised in hearts and ears and accuses them of resisting the Holy Spirit, using the same bodily image for resistance.

source.text: To whom shall I speak and testify, and he will hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the Lord’s utterance became a reproach to them; they certainly will not wish to hear it.
source.display_text: To whom shall I speak and testify, and he will hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the Lord’s utterance became a reproach to them; they certainly will not wish to hear it.

targets.text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.
targets.display_text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.

triples.relationship: repeated image of divine fury poured upon the land's inhabitants
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 6 threatens an outpouring of fury across children, young people, men and women, and elders. Jeremiah 7 likewise announces wrath and fury poured upon the place, extending its list from people to livestock, trees and produce.

source.text: And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.
source.display_text: And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.

targets.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, My wrath and fury are poured upon this place, upon the people and the livestock, upon every tree of their field and all the earth’s produce; and it will burn and not be extinguished.
targets.display_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, My wrath and fury are poured upon this place, upon the people and the livestock, upon every tree of their field and all the earth’s produce; and it will burn and not be extinguished.

triples.relationship: parallel dispossession of houses, fields and families
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces that houses, fields and wives will pass to others. Deuteronomy's curse similarly describes another man taking a wife, a builder not occupying his house and strangers consuming the land's produce and receiving the children.

source.text: And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.
source.display_text: And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.

targets.text: You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.
Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.

triples.relationship: parallel corruption reaching priests and prophets
triples.rationale: Jeremiah's charge of widespread lawless deeds expressly includes priests and false prophets. Micah likewise indicts leaders, priests and prophets for distorted justice and paid religious activity; its list supplies particular leadership examples rather than Jeremiah's small-to-great formula.

source.text: For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
source.display_text: For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.

targets.text: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,
targets.display_text: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,

targets.text: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!
targets.display_text: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!

targets.text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
targets.display_text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”

triples.relationship: parallel false proclamation of peace where there is none
triples.rationale: Jeremiah condemns dismissive treatment of the people's fracture with the cry of peace and asks where peace is. Ezekiel explicitly describes prophets misleading the people by saying peace when there is no peace, then develops the image of a coated wall.

source.text: And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?
source.display_text: And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

targets.text: Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,
targets.display_text: Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

triples.relationship: recurring indictment of shamelessness
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 6 says the people failed yet did not feel shame or recognize dishonor. Jeremiah 3 similarly calls the addressee shameless in its prostitution imagery; the later verse adds the threatened fall at visitation.

source.text: They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.
source.display_text: They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.

targets.text: You had many shepherds as a stumbling block for yourself. You had a prostitute’s appearance; you were shameless toward everyone.
targets.display_text: You had many shepherds as a stumbling block for yourself. You had a prostitute’s appearance; you were shameless toward everyone.

triples.relationship: recurring ancient-road imagery amid refusal of God's way
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 6 calls for the Lord's eternal paths and the good way, but receives refusal. Jeremiah 18 joins forgetting God with weakness in the people's ways, the age-old tracks, and stepping upon paths with no road for travel; both connect the road imagery with failed fidelity, without substituting rest for Jeremiah 6's purification.

source.text: Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the roads and see, and ask for the Lord’s eternal paths and see which is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find purification for your souls. And they said, ‘We will not go.’
source.display_text: Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the roads and see, and ask for the Lord’s eternal paths and see which is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find purification for your souls. And they said, ‘We will not go.’

targets.display_text: Because My people forgot Me, they burned incense in vain; and they will become weak in their ways, the age-old tracks, to step upon paths having no road for travel,

triples.relationship: parallel ignored warning trumpet from an appointed watcher
triples.rationale: Jeremiah reports God's appointment of watchers and the people's refusal to hear the trumpet. Ezekiel describes an appointed watchman sounding a trumpet and a hearer who fails to heed it and is overtaken by the sword.

source.text: I have appointed watchers over you: Hear the trumpet’s sound! And they said, ‘We will not hear.’
source.display_text: I have appointed watchers over you: Hear the trumpet’s sound! And they said, ‘We will not hear.’

targets.display_text: and a hearer hears the trumpet’s sound but does not take care, and the sword comes upon him and overtakes him, his blood will be upon his own head.

targets.text: Because he heard the trumpet’s sound and did not take care, his blood will be upon himself. But this one, because he took care, rescued his life.
targets.display_text: Because he heard the trumpet’s sound and did not take care, his blood will be upon himself. But this one, because he took care, rescued his life.

triples.relationship: parallel rejection of instruction yielding the fruit of one's own way
triples.rationale: Jeremiah calls the coming evils the fruit of turning away because the people rejected God's words and law. Wisdom's speech in Proverbs likewise joins rejected wisdom, counsel and reproof with eating the fruits of one's own way.

source.text: Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.
source.display_text: Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.

targets.text: for they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
targets.display_text: for they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord,

targets.text: nor did they want to attend to my counsels, but they were sneering at my reproofs.
targets.display_text: nor did they want to attend to my counsels, but they were sneering at my reproofs.

targets.text: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.
targets.display_text: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.

triples.relationship: parallel rejection of incense and sacrifices from a culpable people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says imported incense, burnt offerings and sacrifices do not please God. Isaiah likewise refuses burnt offerings and calls incense an abomination while exposing blood-filled hands; neither passage treats costly ritual gifts as a substitute for rectitude.

source.text: Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.
source.display_text: Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.

targets.display_text: “What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,

targets.text: not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
targets.display_text: not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,

targets.display_text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.

triples.relationship: parallel arrival of peoples summoned from distant extremities
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces a people from the north and nations roused from the earth's extremity. Isaiah likewise describes a signal raised among distant nations and a whistle from the earth's end for their rapid arrival; it does not repeat the northern direction.

source.text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.
source.display_text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.

targets.display_text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!

triples.rationale: Jeremiah depicts bows, spears, horses and chariots with a voice like a surging sea. Isaiah likewise describes bows, horses and chariot wheels and then a cry like a surging sea; this preserves the target's unresolved pronoun rather than forcing one actor onto every clause.

source.text: They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.
source.display_text: They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.

targets.text: Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.
targets.display_text: Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.

targets.text: They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.
targets.display_text: They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.

targets.text: It will cry out because of them on that day like the sound of a surging sea. They will look to the earth, and behold, harsh darkness in their perplexity.
targets.display_text: It will cry out because of them on that day like the sound of a surging sea. They will look to the earth, and behold, harsh darkness in their perplexity.

triples.relationship: parallel disabling distress compared with childbirth
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 6 describes paralyzed hands and labor pains after hearing the invasion report. Jeremiah 4 likewise depicts Zion fainting, letting her hands fall and groaning like a woman in labor over those killed.

source.text: We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.
source.display_text: We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.

targets.text: For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!
targets.display_text: For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!
