triples.relationship: parallel repeated early sending of prophets to an unresponsive people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah describes the sending of God's servants the prophets by day and at dawn over Israel's history. Chronicles likewise describes God rising early and sending prophetic messengers whom the people scorned, without reproducing Jeremiah's exodus-to-present span.

source.text: From the day their fathers left Egypt’s land until this day, I sent out to you all My servants the prophets by day and at dawn, and I sent them.
source.display_text: From the day their fathers left Egypt’s land until this day, I sent out to you all My servants the prophets by day and at dawn, and I sent them.

targets.text: The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
targets.display_text: The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.

targets.text: They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.
targets.display_text: They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

triples.relationship: parallel inherited resistance to divine instruction
triples.rationale: Jeremiah indicts unhearing ears and a neck hardened beyond the fathers'. Acts similarly charges stiff-necked, uncircumcised hearers with resisting as their fathers did and failing to keep the received law; beyond and as are distinct comparisons.

source.text: And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.
source.display_text: And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.

targets.text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.
targets.display_text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.

targets.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become—
targets.display_text: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become—

targets.text: you who received the law through the ordinances of angels and did not keep it.”
targets.display_text: you who received the law through the ordinances of angels and did not keep it.”

triples.relationship: parallel failure of truth and recognition of God among the people
triples.rationale: The composite source unit describes a nation refusing God's voice and instruction, with faithfulness failing from its mouth. Hosea likewise charges the land with no truth or recognition of God and explicitly lists falsehood among its offenses, giving a concrete social counterpart to the failed speech.

source.text: And you will say this word to them: This is the nation that did not hear the Lord’s voice or accept instruction; faithfulness failed from their mouth.
source.display_text: And you will say this word to them: This is the nation that did not hear the Lord’s voice or accept instruction; faithfulness failed from their mouth.

targets.text: Hear the Lord’s word, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the land’s inhabitants: there is no truth, no mercy and no recognition of God upon the land.
targets.display_text: Hear the Lord’s word, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the land’s inhabitants: there is no truth, no mercy and no recognition of God upon the land.

targets.text: Cursing, falsehood, murder, theft and adultery have poured over the land, and they mix bloodshed with bloodshed.
targets.display_text: Cursing, falsehood, murder, theft and adultery have poured over the land, and they mix bloodshed with bloodshed.

triples.relationship: parallel hair cutting as mourning for national loss
triples.rationale: Jeremiah commands shearing the head and taking up lament because God rejected the generation. Micah likewise commands shaving and shearing for children taken captive, using a corresponding mourning action with a specified loss.

source.text: Shear your head and cast it away, and take up a lament on your lips, because the Lord rejected and thrust away the generation doing these things.
source.display_text: Shear your head and cast it away, and take up a lament on your lips, because the Lord rejected and thrust away the generation doing these things.

targets.text: Shave yourself and shear your hair for your delicate children. Enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, for they have been taken captive away from you.
targets.display_text: Shave yourself and shear your hair for your delicate children. Enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, for they have been taken captive away from you.

triples.relationship: historical counterpart to abominations placed in God's named house
triples.rationale: Jeremiah charges Judah with setting abominations in the house bearing God's name. Kings records Manasseh's altars and carved grove image in that house and repeatedly recalls God's placing His name there, giving a particular historical example of the profanation.

source.text: For Judah’s sons did evil before Me, says the Lord; they set their abominations in the house over which My name has been called, to defile it.
source.display_text: For Judah’s sons did evil before Me, says the Lord; they set their abominations in the house over which My name has been called, to defile it.

targets.text: He built an altar in the Lord’s house, as He had said, ‘In Jerusalem I shall place My name.’
targets.display_text: He built an altar in the Lord’s house, as He had said, ‘In Jerusalem I shall place My name.’

targets.text: He built an altar for all heaven’s host in the two courts of the Lord’s house.
targets.display_text: He built an altar for all heaven’s host in the two courts of the Lord’s house.

targets.text: He led his sons through fire, practiced divination from sounds, read omens, and appointed a charmer and knowing ones. He did much evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
targets.display_text: He led his sons through fire, practiced divination from sounds, read omens, and appointed a charmer and knowing ones. He did much evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.

targets.text: He placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David and his son Solomon, ‘In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all Israel’s tribes, I shall place My name there for ever.
targets.display_text: He placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David and his son Solomon, ‘In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all Israel’s tribes, I shall place My name there for ever.

triples.relationship: legal condemnation corresponding to burning children for gods
triples.rationale: Jeremiah condemns burning sons and daughters at Topheth as something God did not command. Deuteronomy forbids imitating the nations' worship and explicitly says they burn sons and daughters for their gods, acts the Lord hates.

source.text: And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.
source.display_text: And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.

targets.text: And if the Lord your God destroys from before you the nations whither you go to inherit their land, and you inherit their possession and dwell in their land,

take heed unto yourself, that you do not seek to follow them after they have been destroyed from before you. You shall not inquire after their gods, saying: How do these nations serve their gods? I also will do so.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did unto their gods, for they burn their sons and their daughters with fire unto their gods.

triples.relationship: historical connection through Topheth and the Hinnom ravine
triples.rationale: Jeremiah predicts that Topheth and the ravine of Hinnom's son will be renamed for the slain. Kings names Tapheth in the valley of Ennom's son when describing Josiah's defilement of the site and mentions children and fire; it provides the corresponding location with variant name forms, not an account of the predicted renaming.

source.text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.
source.display_text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.

targets.text: He defiled Tapheth in the valley of the son of Ennom, for a man to lead his son, and a man his daughter, through fire to Moloch.
targets.display_text: He defiled Tapheth in the valley of the son of Ennom, for a man to lead his son, and a man his daughter, through fire to Moloch.

triples.relationship: repeated curse of corpses exposed to birds and beasts
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says the people's dead will feed heaven's birds and earth's beasts with no one to drive them away. Deuteronomy's curse states the same combination of exposed dead, scavengers and absence of anyone to drive them off.

source.text: And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.
source.display_text: And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

targets.text: And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to drive them away.

triples.relationship: repeated removal of joy and wedding voices
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 7 announces the ending of gladness and the voices of bridegroom and bride in Judah and Jerusalem. Jeremiah 16 repeats that specific list of silenced celebrations and adds that it will occur before the hearers' eyes and in their days.

source.text: And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.
source.display_text: And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.

targets.text: Because thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, before your eyes and in your days I am stopping from this place the sound of joy and rejoicing, the voice of bridegroom and bride.
targets.display_text: Because thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, before your eyes and in your days I am stopping from this place the sound of joy and rejoicing, the voice of bridegroom and bride.

triples.relationship: restoration reversing the silencing of wedding and joyful voices
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 7 threatens the removal of joy and bridegroom and bride voices as the land becomes desolate. Jeremiah 40 promises that these same sounds will again be heard in the deserted cities and Jerusalem's surroundings, providing an explicit reversal through restoration.

source.text: And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.
source.display_text: And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.

targets.display_text: Thus said the Lord: Again in this place, which you call deserted of people and animals, in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, desolate because there are no people or animals, there will be heard

They will bring gifts into the Lord’s house, for I will bring back all the exiles of that land as before, said the Lord.
targets.display_text: the sound of joy and rejoicing, the bridegroom’s voice and the bride’s voice, the voices of those saying, Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good; His mercy is for ever. They will bring gifts into the Lord’s house, for I will bring back all the exiles of that land as before, said the Lord.

triples.relationship: related removal of bones from tombs in an idolatry-judgment setting
triples.rationale: Jeremiah threatens exposure of the bones of rulers, priests, prophets and Jerusalem's inhabitants. Kings likewise records bones taken from tombs during Josiah's judgment upon an idolatrous altar, but with a different agent, purpose and group rather than as fulfillment of Jeremiah's threat.

source.text: At that time, says the Lord, they will bring the bones of Judah’s kings and the bones of its rulers and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those dwelling in Jerusalem out of their tombs,
source.display_text: At that time, says the Lord, they will bring the bones of Judah’s kings and the bones of its rulers and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those dwelling in Jerusalem out of their tombs,

targets.text: Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city. He sent and took the bones from the tombs, burned them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the Lord’s word which the man of God spoke while Jeroboam stood at the festival beside the altar. Turning, he lifted his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.
targets.display_text: Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city. triples.relationship: prohibition underlying the charge of worshiping heaven's bodies
triples.rationale: Jeremiah lists sun, moon, stars and heaven's host as objects the people loved, served and worshiped. Deuteronomy specifically warns against being led to bow to and serve the sun, moon, stars and heaven's adornment, identifying the forbidden worship behind the exposure of their bones.

source.text: and expose them to cool before the sun and moon and all the stars and all heaven’s host, which they loved and served and followed and clung to and bowed down to. They will not be mourned or buried, and they will be an example upon the earth’s surface,
source.display_text: and expose them to cool before the sun and moon and all the stars and all heaven’s host, which they loved and served and followed and clung to and bowed down to. They will not be mourned or buried, and they will be an example upon the earth’s surface,

targets.text: And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and all the adornment of heaven, and be led astray to bow down unto them and serve them, which the Lord your God has allotted unto all the nations under heaven.

triples.relationship: contrast with the command to choose life
triples.rationale: Jeremiah says they chose death rather than life in the account of judgment and dispersal. Deuteronomy sets the same alternatives before Israel and commands choosing life through love and obedience to God; Jeremiah describes the judged generation, whereas Deuteronomy exhorts those entering the land.

source.text: because they chose death rather than life, and for all the remnants left from that generation in every place where I drive them away.
source.display_text: because they chose death rather than life, and for all the remnants left from that generation in every place where I drive them away.

targets.text: I call heaven and earth to witness unto you this day: I have set before your face life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, that you and your seed may live,

to love the Lord your God, to obey His voice, and to cleave unto Him; for this is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them.

triples.relationship: parallel expectation of rising after a fall
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks whether one who falls does not rise as an analogy preceding the charge of refusal to return. Proverbs likewise says the righteous fall seven times and rise, though Jeremiah's rhetorical question is not restricted to the proverb's righteous person.

source.text: For thus says the Lord: Does one who falls not rise? Or does one who turns away not return?
source.display_text: For thus says the Lord: Does one who falls not rise? Or does one who turns away not return?

targets.text: for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.
targets.display_text: for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.

triples.relationship: repeated accusation of stubborn refusal to return
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 describes the people held fast in their choice and unwilling to return. Jeremiah 5 likewise says their faces were hardened beyond rock and they would not return despite discipline, repeating the resistance through different images.

source.text: Why has this people of Mine turned away with a shameless turning away, and been held fast in their own choice, and been unwilling to return?
source.display_text: Why has this people of Mine turned away with a shameless turning away, and been held fast in their own choice, and been unwilling to return?

targets.text: Lord, Thine eyes are toward faithfulness. Thou didst scourge them, and they did not suffer; Thou broughtest them to an end, and they would not accept instruction. They hardened their faces beyond rock and would not return.
targets.display_text: Lord, Thine eyes are toward faithfulness. Thou didst scourge them, and they did not suffer; Thou broughtest them to an end, and they would not accept instruction. They hardened their faces beyond rock and would not return.

triples.relationship: contrast between absent repentance and actual turning from lawlessness
triples.rationale: Jeremiah finds no one repenting or asking what he has done. Ezekiel describes a lawless person turning to judgment and righteousness and calls Israel to turn from impieties, presenting the response missing in Jeremiah without attempting to equate the horse image.

source.text: Give ear now and hear: they will not speak thus; there is no person repenting of his evil, saying, ‘What have I done?’ The runner ceased from his course like a sweating horse in its neighing.
source.display_text: Give ear now and hear: they will not speak thus; there is no person repenting of his evil, saying, ‘What have I done?’ The runner ceased from his course like a sweating horse in its neighing.

targets.text: When a lawless person turns from the lawlessness he practiced and practices judgment and righteousness, this one has preserved his life
targets.display_text: When a lawless person turns from the lawlessness he practiced and practices judgment and righteousness, this one has preserved his life

targets.text: and turned from all the impieties he committed; he will surely live, he certainly will not die.
targets.display_text: and turned from all the impieties he committed; he will surely live, he certainly will not die.

targets.text: The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?
targets.display_text: The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?

targets.text: I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
targets.display_text: I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.

triples.relationship: parallel comparison of knowledgeable animals with an unknowing people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah contrasts birds knowing their seasons with the people's ignorance of the Lord's judgments. Isaiah likewise contrasts an ox and donkey knowing their keeper or manger with Israel's failure to know God, using different animal knowledge to expose the same human failure.

source.text: Even the stork in heaven knew her time; turtledove and swallow, field sparrows, kept the times of their coming, but My people did not know the Lord’s judgments.
source.display_text: Even the stork in heaven knew her time; turtledove and swallow, field sparrows, kept the times of their coming, but My people did not know the Lord’s judgments.

targets.text: An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
targets.display_text: An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”

triples.relationship: contrast between rejecting divine speech and the foundation of wisdom
triples.rationale: Jeremiah questions what wisdom remains in those who rejected the Lord's word. Proverbs places wisdom and perception in fear and reverence toward God and calls the ungodly despisers of wisdom and discipline, showing why rejection of divine instruction undermines a claim to wisdom.

source.text: The wise were ashamed and terrified and captured, because they rejected the Lord’s word. What wisdom is in them?
source.display_text: The wise were ashamed and terrified and captured, because they rejected the Lord’s word. What wisdom is in them?

targets.text: The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
targets.display_text: The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.

triples.relationship: repeated transfer of wives and fields to others
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 announces wives given to others and fields to inheritors. Jeremiah 6 repeats the transfer of fields and wives along with houses and explicitly identifies it as God's action against the land's inhabitants.

source.text: Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to inheritors,
source.display_text: Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to inheritors,

targets.text: And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.
targets.display_text: And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: parallel failure of vine and fig produce with a different response
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces no grapes on vines and no figs on fig trees, with fallen leaves. Habakkuk likewise anticipates fruitless figs and unproductive vines but answers with rejoicing in God, a response Jeremiah's agricultural description does not supply.

source.text: and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.
source.display_text: and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.

targets.display_text: For the fig tree will not bear fruit, and vines will have no produce; the olive’s labor will fail, and fields will not produce food. Sheep have failed for lack of food, and there are no cattle at feeding troughs.

targets.text: But I will exult in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Savior.
targets.display_text: But I will exult in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Savior.

triples.relationship: repeated gall-water punishment explained by disobedience
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 says God gave gall-water because the people sinned before Him. Jeremiah 9 likewise threatens gall-water after describing abandonment of God's law, refusal to hear and following the evil heart and idols.

source.text: Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.
source.display_text: Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.

triples.relationship: parallel disappointed expectation of peace and healing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 reports gathering for peace without good things and for healing only to find haste. Jeremiah 14 repeats the expectation of peace and healing with no good things but turmoil; haste and turmoil are retained as different supplied outcomes.

source.text: We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!
source.display_text: We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!

targets.text: Hast Thou utterly rejected Judah, and has Thy soul departed from Zion? Why didst Thou strike us, and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, turmoil!
targets.display_text: Hast Thou utterly rejected Judah, and has Thy soul departed from Zion? Why didst Thou strike us, and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, turmoil!

triples.relationship: repeated threatening sound from Dan
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 places the alarming sound of invading horses at Dan. Jeremiah 4 similarly expects a voice announcing from Dan and trouble from Ephraim; the geographical alarm recurs without equating the announcer's voice with the horses themselves.

source.text: From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.
source.display_text: From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.

targets.text: For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.
targets.display_text: For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.

triples.relationship: parallel sending of deadly serpents among a sinful people
triples.rationale: Jeremiah announces deadly snakes that cannot be charmed and will bite. Numbers likewise records the Lord sending deadly serpents that bite the people, followed by confession; the healing that follows there is not promised in Jeremiah's warning.

source.text: Because behold, I am sending out among you deadly snakes that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.
source.display_text: Because behold, I am sending out among you deadly snakes that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.

targets.text: And the Lord sent deadly serpents among the people. They bit the people, and many of the sons of Israel died.

And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpents from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.

triples.relationship: related appeal to divine presence amid deserved calamity
triples.rationale: Jeremiah hears the question whether the Lord and a king are in Zion and then gives God's charge concerning carved and futile things. Micah likewise exposes an appeal to the Lord's presence as supposed protection from calamity and announces Jerusalem's ruin; the latter's confident claim differs from Jeremiah's anguished question.

source.text: Behold, the crying voice of the daughter of My people from a distant land: ‘Is the Lord not in Zion? Is a King not there?’ Why did they provoke Me with their carved things and foreign futile things?
source.display_text: Behold, the crying voice of the daughter of My people from a distant land: ‘Is the Lord not in Zion? Is a King not there?’ Why did they provoke Me with their carved things and foreign futile things?

targets.text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
targets.display_text: Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”

targets.text: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.
targets.display_text: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.

triples.relationship: parallel labor-pain image for distress over the people's destruction
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 describes being overcome by labor-like pains at the crushing of the people's daughter. Jeremiah 4 likewise gives Zion a voice like a woman in labor and failing strength over those killed, linking the birth-pain imagery with the national disaster.

source.text: At the crushing of the daughter of My people I was darkened; in bewilderment, pains like a woman giving birth overpowered me.
source.display_text: At the crushing of the daughter of My people I was darkened; in bewilderment, pains like a woman giving birth overpowered me.

targets.text: For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!
targets.display_text: For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!

triples.relationship: parallel Gilead resin and remedies failing to bring healing
triples.rationale: Jeremiah 8 asks about resin and a physician in Gilead and the people's missing healing. Jeremiah 26 addresses Gilead and calls for resin for Egypt while declaring multiplied remedies vain and without benefit, repeating the named medicine and failed benefit for a different people.

source.text: Is there no resin in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why did healing not rise for the daughter of My people?
source.display_text: Is there no resin in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why did healing not rise for the daughter of My people?

triples.relationship: parallel tears flowing from the eyes over the people's shattering
triples.rationale: Jeremiah asks for a watery head and fountain-like eyes to weep day and night for the wounded people. Lamentations likewise describes the eye bringing down outpourings of water over the shattering of the people's daughter; the speaker then will not be silent because there is no recovery.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit is only the introductory word-coming formula. The particular content of the commission is reviewed in the following units; another generic revelation formula would not provide a sufficiently particular connection for this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying, What do you see, Jeremiah? I said, A nut-wood staff.
deferred_source_units.reason: The supplied vision names a nut-wood staff. No verified counterpart establishes the significance of this particular object, and the performance promise in 1:12 does not justify substituting a familiar almond formulation or importing another staff narrative.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Hear the Lord’s word, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit summons Jacob and every Israelite clan to hear. Its particular indictment follows in 2:5; another broad summons to hear would mainly repeat an introductory form without a further supported connection.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully. See whether such things have happened.
deferred_source_units.reason: The command to inspect Kittim and Kedar introduces the comparison of exchanged gods in 2:11. No particular counterpart for this two-location investigation has been established, and the following supported comparison does not automatically complete this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes knew you and mocked you.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual verse says the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes knew and mocked the addressee. A parallel about Egypt shaving or breaking a crown would replace its supplied action; no precise counterpart to this named mockery is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: How will you say, I was not polluted and did not follow Baal? See your ways in the burial ground and know what you did. Late her voice wailed; her ways
deferred_source_units.reason: The denial of Baal pollution leads into a burial-ground reference and the unusual connected clause about a late-wailing voice and her ways. Read together with 2:24, these words do not support substituting the familiar camel imagery or assigning a secure particular counterpart to the complete unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: she broadened upon wilderness waters. In her soul’s desires she was carried by the wind; she was handed over. Who will turn her back? All who seek her will not toil; in her humiliation they will find her.
deferred_source_units.reason: The connected description speaks of broadened ways upon wilderness waters, desire, wind, being handed over and discovery in humiliation. No securely read target clarifies this full combination; familiar wild-donkey or mating-season wording is absent and cannot be substituted.

deferred_source_units.source_text: As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the sons of Israel will be ashamed: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests and their prophets.
deferred_source_units.reason: The particular comparison is shame like that of a caught thief, extended to Israel and its leaders. The read Proverbs thief passage concerns appetite and restitution rather than shame, while the Isaiah shame passage lacks the caught-thief comparison; both candidates remain unretained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Why do you speak to Me? All of you acted ungodly, and all of you acted lawlessly against Me, says the Lord.
deferred_source_units.reason: The question asks why the people speak to God and then charges everyone with ungodliness and lawlessness. No sufficiently particular counterpart to this question and accusation is established; a generic corporate confession would change the rhetorical situation.

deferred_source_units.source_text: What good practice will you still pursue in your ways to seek love? Not so; you too acted wickedly to pollute your ways.
deferred_source_units.reason: The rhetorical question about pursuing good practice to seek love is followed by polluted ways. The supplied phrasing does not warrant importing a claim that the woman teaches other evil women, and no precise target for its actual question is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Will He remain for ever, or will it be guarded always? Behold, you spoke and did these evil things and were able.
deferred_source_units.reason: The questions ask whether He remains forever or whether it is guarded always, without naming anger as the object. A target about anger not lasting forever would supply an unstated noun; the subsequent charge of effective evil does not resolve that wording sufficiently for a retained pair.

deferred_source_units.source_text: When you multiply and increase upon the land in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, The ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel. It will not come to mind, be named or be attended to, and it will not be made again.
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit specifically predicts the ark no longer being recalled, named, attended to or made again. General descriptions of the ark or a new covenant would not themselves establish this particular cessation claim; no verified direct counterpart is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: At that time they will say to this people and Jerusalem: A spirit of wandering in the wilderness; the daughter of My people’s way is not toward purity or holiness.
deferred_source_units.reason: The supplied image is a spirit of wandering in the wilderness and a way lacking purity or holiness. No definite counterpart is established, and a familiar hot wind used for winnowing would import absent wording.

deferred_source_units.source_text: A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit speaks of a spirit of filling coming to the speaker while the speaker now announces judgments. Its precise image is unresolved in the supplied text; no target is retained on the basis of an assumed strong-wind reading.

deferred_source_units.source_text: All are strong,
deferred_source_units.reason: The whole unit is All are strong, referring through context to the invading nation. A generic description of another strong army would add little beyond that broad military trait, so the actual short unit remains pending separately from supported 5:15 and 5:17.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Announce these things to the house of Jacob, and let it be heard in Judah.
deferred_source_units.reason: This is an announcement instruction to Jacob and Judah without the subsequent accusation itself. No particular connection beyond the generic two-house address has been retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Astonishment and horrifying things happened upon the land:
deferred_source_units.reason: This introductory line announces astonishment and horrifying things on the land. The particular corruption is specified in 5:31 and reviewed there; a general horror announcement would not independently substantiate this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: and your height will be taken away, daughter of Zion.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual line says Zion will have her height taken away. No precise counterpart establishes the sense of this height in the siege setting, and familiar descriptions of a beautiful or luxuriant daughter are not present in this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: As a cistern cools water, so her evil cools; impiety and misery will be heard in her, continually before her. With pain and scourging
deferred_source_units.reason: The comparison says a cistern cools water and her evil cools, then continues into pain and scourging. No precise target clarifies this unusual cooling image; a spring constantly pouring out wickedness would substitute another wording.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Therefore the nations heard, and those shepherding their flocks.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit says nations and those shepherding their flocks heard, without specifying a separate response. The adjoining announcement in 6:19 is supported, but a broad appeal to nations would not establish a particular counterpart for this short hearing clause.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am placing weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will become weak in it; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.
deferred_source_units.reason: God places weakness upon the people, and fathers, sons and neighbors weaken or perish together. The supplied image is weakness rather than a stumbling stone; no distinct, sufficiently close counterpart to the combined formulation is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Hear the Lord’s word, all Judea!
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual unit is the brief summons for all Judea to hear the Lord. The ethical and temple-specific content follows in later units, and another generic hearing summons would not provide a particular connection for this one.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Do you not see what they are doing in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets?
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit asks whether the addressee sees what is happening in Judah and Jerusalem. The observed family ritual is specified and supported in 7:18; the question alone has no separately verified counterpart.

deferred_source_units.source_text: How will you say, ‘We are wise, and the Lord’s law is with us’? A false reed-pen came to be in vain for scribes.
deferred_source_units.reason: The claim to wisdom and possession of the law is challenged by a false reed-pen being in vain for scribes. The read Jeremiah 23:36 lacks the familiar clause about perverting divine words and does not mention scribal writing, so it does not substantiate the proposed particular connection.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Incurable things, with pain, while your heart is bewildered.
deferred_source_units.reason: The fragment speaks of incurable things, pain and a bewildered heart after the snake warning. Its precise scope is uncertain; a generic lament about an individual wound would risk assigning a subject and injury that this unit does not specify.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Summer passed, harvest went by, and we were not delivered.
deferred_source_units.reason: The lament specifically contrasts passed summer and harvest with continued nondeliverance. No verified target shares this seasonal delay pattern closely enough; a generic missed-opportunity or final-harvest analogy would change the time frame and claim.

But if caught, he will repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he will rescue himself.
